decisions.context: Weekly store and product forecasts need repeatable stages, while new model ideas should reach production quickly. The workflow must make a missed or failed stage visible before it disrupts the weekly run.

alternatives.label: Orchestrated ML pipeline
pros: Fast iteration: connected training and evaluation

decisions.rationale: Past-week reproducibility and protection of the weekly run decide the choice: orchestration makes the stages repeatable. It costs more setup than manual scripts.
consequences: Pipeline stages and dependencies need maintenance.
Failures can be isolated to stages for reruns.

decisions.context: Reproducing any past forecast requires knowing which input data, pipeline, experiment, and model produced it. The brief makes this traceability a core requirement.

alternatives.label: End-to-end reproducible lifecycle governance
pros: Reproducibility: links data, runs, artifacts, and health
cons: Small-team cost: broad governance to maintain

decisions.rationale: Past-week reproducibility decides the choice because it requires linking datasets, runs, and models across the lifecycle. The trade-off is extra tracking and governance work for a three-person team.
consequences: Retain dataset snapshots or versions and run metadata.
Keep pipeline, dependency, and model versions associated with each forecast.

decisions.context: Past forecasts cannot be reconstructed if historical inputs or their provenance are lost. Preserving original data supports replay and comparison.

alternatives.label: Traceable and preserved data
pros: Reproducibility: provenance and original data retained

alternatives.label: Cataloged data
pros: Fast investigation: profiles and versions discoverable
cons: Reproducibility: catalog alone may not preserve original inputs

decisions.rationale: Past-week reproducibility decides the choice: retaining provenance and original inputs enables recovery of the data used for a forecast. This adds storage and retention work.
consequences: Historical inputs need retention and access controls.

decisions.context: New models need a quick path to production, but must not jeopardize the weekly forecast run. Evaluation should catch a quality regression before promotion.

alternatives.label: Threshold-based quality regression testing
pros: Protect weekly run: blocks threshold regressions

alternatives.label: Offline evaluation pipeline
pros: Forecast quality: tests against held-out data
cons: Protect weekly run: does not itself define a regression threshold

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: a candidate should fail promotion when it crosses a quality regression threshold. Thresholds need to be selected and maintained for the forecasting objective.
consequences: Failed candidates leave the production model unchanged.

decisions.context: Model ideas can change data preparation, training, and evaluation components. Validating the full pipeline helps detect breaks before a candidate affects the weekly run.

alternatives.label: Automated full-pipeline integration testing
pros: Protect weekly run: exercises connected stages
cons: Compute cost: full pipeline runs consume resources

alternatives.label: Training health validation
pros: Protect weekly run: detects unhealthy training
cons: Coverage: does not validate all pipeline stages

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: exercising the connected workflow can catch integration failures before promotion. The cost is additional compute and maintenance for test runs.
consequences: Maintain representative test data and pipeline checks.
Schedule validation so it does not compete with the weekly production run.

decisions.context: The system produces forecasts weekly per store and product; the brief does not require request-time predictions. Batch computation fits the stated cadence and allows forecasts to be stored for use.

alternatives.label: Scheduled batch prediction deployment
pros: Reproducibility: results can be stored by run
cons: Freshness: results wait for the next batch

alternatives.label: Online computation serving
cons: Weekly cadence: adds runtime serving complexity

decisions.rationale: The weekly cadence decides the choice: scheduled batch scoring matches the stated forecast cycle and avoids unnecessary online serving complexity. The trade-off is that forecasts update on the schedule rather than on demand.
consequences: Persist forecast outputs with their run and model versions.
Provide downstream users a stable location for each weekly forecast set.

decisions.context: A team of three data scientists owns the pipeline end to end and wants model ideas to reach production quickly. Short cycles support experimentation, while automated checks and release controls protect the weekly run.

alternatives.label: Lean iterative ML development
cons: Protect weekly run: needs release safeguards

alternatives.label: Cross-functional ML delivery team
pros: Protect weekly run: combines delivery skills
cons: Small team ownership: requires additional roles

decisions.rationale: Fast model iteration decides the choice, given the small team and the request to move ideas quickly. The team must pair short cycles with the pipeline validation and rollback controls captured in other decisions.
consequences: Deliver candidate improvements in small increments.
Keep production promotion behind validation gates.

uncovered: Forecast model family and forecasting objective, including seasonality and store/product hierarchy.
Exact weekly schedule, data arrival cutoff, and recovery procedure for a missed run.
Evaluation metrics, acceptance thresholds, and business impact measures for retail demand.
Data-source ingestion mechanism and handling of late or corrected sales data.
Compute infrastructure, storage technology, retention duration, and access policy.
